source_row.rationale: Severe decompensated hypothyroidism with hypothermia, bradycardia, and major alteration in mental status is characteristic of myxedema coma, so Option B is correct. Adrenal crisis and septic shock can cause hemodynamic instability but do not specifically match this severe hypothyroid pattern. Thyroid storm is severe thyrotoxicosis and typically produces the opposite hyperadrenergic pattern.
source_row.source_detail: StatPearls Myxedema Coma — History and Physical/Evaluation: decompensated severe hypothyroidism typically features altered mental status and hypothermia, with bradycardia, hypotension or hypoventilation and multisystem dysfunction; it is a life-threatening endocrine emergency. StatPearls Myxedema Coma updated 2025-12-13 and current in StatPearls [Internet] 2026; NCBI source live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, endocrine/vascular emergencies and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client with severe untreated hypothyroidism develops hypothermia, bradycardia, and a markedly decreased level of consciousness. Which complication is most likely?
